floor_history.headline: Recon s1: canonical island respell (func_800274BC form) lowered floor 33->30 with insn parity 144==144; full residual map banked; disc-copy survival is the frontier head.

s1 frontier head CLOSED: combine (not cse) folds the disc copy; an if/else-spelled LZCS guard makes it survive at zero insn cost, landing in $a0 (target's register) in the beqz delay slot. Floor still

Floor 30 -> 7 at unchanged parity 144==144: reusing sqrt_val in place for the <<9 and naming the first quotient's numerator fixed the entire downstream allocation cascade; residual is 6 slots of disc-

Permuter modality exhausted on the v21 chassis: 33,881 random iterations (zero finds, base never beaten) plus an exhaustive 24-point directed PERM cross-product (none below base) prove floor 7 is a st

Forensics closed the s1-s4 frontier head in closed form: `disc` cannot reach $a2/$6 by allocno priority (would need live_length > 132 in a 144-insn function); the guard's register is chosen by cse.c m

frontier.hypothesis: The 6-slot `disc` residual now needs a NEW CONFLICT EDGE from disc to an early-allocated $5 holder (allocno 123 `result`, or 76/77), simultaneously with keeping allocno 132 (`ud`) alive as the $4 blocker and getting pri(117) below 7273. The priority/live-range axis alone is dead (s5 H5.5); do not re-open it.
frontier.mechanism: global.c find_reg blocks a hard reg only via 117's own hard-reg conflict set or via a reg already held by a CONFLICTING allocno. $2 is already a hard conflict; $3 becomes one once disc is live across the lzcr region (observed in the s5 M1 dump: `;; 117 conflicts: 108 116 117 131 2 3 12 29`); $4 can only come from allocno 132; $5 can only come from 123/76/77 because the one $5 holder disc already conflicts with (116 dist_sq) sits at position 22 and would need live_length > 132.
frontier.next_probe: Attack allocno 123 (`result`). Note that target's `disc < 0` arm is a REAL `return 0;` (`addu $v0,$zero,$zero` + j to the epilogue label past `addu $v0,$a1,$zero`) — i.e. in the original build there is probably NO `result` pseudo on that arm at all, which changes 123's refs/live_length and hence its position AND the disc-vs-result liveness overlap. This makes frontier items (a) and (b) ONE problem, not two: solving slot 88 may be what creates the $5 blocker. Concretely: re-measure the `if (disc < 0) return 0;` spelling (s3 measured it as score 10 via jump2 cross-jump, 142 insns) but this time DUMP it and read (i) the new `;; N regs to allocate` order and 117's conflict set, and (ii) .jump2's find_cross_jump decision, before judging it by score alone. A +3 score that fixes the allocation is a better platform than a flat 7.

frontier.hypothesis: Slot 88: `if (disc < 0) return 0;` produces exactly target's 2-insn block but jump2 cross-jumps it into the entrance return-0 block (142 insns vs target 144), while target and our build BOTH already carry two UN-merged copies of that same block in the entrance chain — so find_cross_jump is selective here and something distinguishes the surviving pair.
frontier.mechanism: jump.c find_cross_jump matches identical instruction tails and redirects the conditional branch to the earlier copy, deleting the block. Whatever property keeps the two entrance copies separate is the property the disc<0 arm must acquire.
frontier.next_probe: The .jump2 slice for the base chassis is ALREADY captured at tmp/grind/func_8002D518/s5/jump2.func.txt (function region, 785 lines) — start there rather than re-dumping. Identify which pair find_cross_jump matched and why the two entrance copies are not merged with each other. Then re-dump with the `if (disc < 0) return 0;` variant applied and diff the two .jump2 regions. Per s4 H13 do NOT spend probes respelling `return 0` itself; the emitted shape is already correct.

frontier.hypothesis: cse.c's make_regs_eqv is now a named, quantified lever for this function and should be consulted BEFORE proposing any spelling that touches the disc/ud pair.
frontier.mechanism: `ud` becomes the quantity's canonical register (and therefore the register every later consumer reads) iff its last use is later than `disc`'s AND it outlives the cse extended basic block. Making `ud`'s last use earlier does not merely change the guard's operand — it deletes allocno 132 outright, because then all of ud's uses are rewritten to disc and the copy has no surviving consumer of its own.
frontier.next_probe: Any future disc/ud spelling must be checked against BOTH conditions before it is built: it must keep `ud`'s last use later than `disc`'s (to preserve allocno 132 as the $4 blocker) while somehow keeping the bltz on `disc`. The only remaining degree of freedom is condition (a) — the cse EXTENDED basic block extent (cse_basic_block_start/end, set by cse_end_of_basic_block under flag_cse_follow_jumps + flag_cse_skip_blocks). If `ud`'s last use can be brought INSIDE the same extended block as the copy while still being later than disc's, the predicate fails on (a) and disc stays canonical WITHOUT losing allocno 132. That is the one untested cell of the 2x2 and it is the highest-value next forensic probe: instrument or read cse.c's block-extent computation for this function and find where the extended block actually ends.
